title: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
tagline: Build the systems that power the modern world, from first principles to artificial intelligence.
overview:
The Bachelor of Science in Computer Science gives you a rigorous foundation in how computation works and the practical skill to build software that matters. You begin by learning to program, then develop the mathematical maturity of discrete math, calculus, and linear algebra that underpins the discipline.

In your second and third years you study the core of the field: data structures and algorithms, computer architecture, operating systems, networks, databases, and software engineering. Your final year brings advanced work in distributed systems and artificial intelligence, electives in areas like cloud computing and natural language processing, and a two-term capstone in which you design and deliver a substantial project of your own.
outcomes: Design, implement, and test correct, efficient, and maintainable software in multiple languages.
Analyze problems mathematically and select appropriate data structures and algorithms.
Explain how computer systems work, from hardware and operating systems to networks and distributed services.
Apply machine learning and AI techniques responsibly, with an understanding of their limits.
Work effectively on software teams using modern engineering practices.
Evaluate the ethical, legal, and social implications of computing.
